person_note: The diagnostic Goodreads passages place Hester and Wilde under external third-person narration, while first- and second-person forms elsewhere occur in dialogue, free-indirect thought, or generic aphorisms. An authorized opening and a separate authorized interior excerpt independently sustain third-person narration, and the whole-book point-of-view guide explicitly describes a third-person narrator whose focus moves among Wilde, Matthew, and Hester. No credible evidence indicates sustained narration in another person; the main limitation is that the authorized prose sources are excerpts rather than the complete novel.
